# Configuring a Local LLM Provider

Point your terminal app at an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (e.g., Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM) by adding an `[llm]` section to your TOML config file:
```toml[llm]
provider = "openai"
base_url = "http://localhost:11434/v1"
model = "llama3"
api_key = "not-needed"
```
- **provider** — The API flavor. Use `"openai"` for any OpenAI-compatible server.
- **base_url** — The full HTTP(S) address of your local endpoint. Common defaults: `http://localhost:11434/v1` (Ollama), `http://localhost:8080/v1` (LM Studio).
- **model** — The model name the server exposes. Run `curl http://localhost:11434/v1/models` to list available models.
- **api_key** — Many local servers ignore this value; `"not-needed"` works in most cases. If your server requires a key, supply it here.

After editing, restart the terminal app so it picks up the new configuration.

## Troubleshooting
| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `connection refused` | Ensure the local server is running and `base_url` matches its bind address and port. |
| `model not found` | Verify the model name against the server's `/v1/models` endpoint; some servers require the full tag (e.g., `llama3:instruct`). |
| `401 / unauthorized` | Set `api_key` to the value your server expects. |
| `404 / no route` | Check that `base_url` ends with `/v1` (or the correct API prefix for your server). |
| Slow responses | Try a smaller model, reduce `max_tokens`, or increase the server's context window. |
| Config changes ignored | Restart the app; some editors cache TOML files. Run `cat ~/.config/app/config.toml` to confirm the file was saved. |
| SSL errors with HTTPS | Set `verify_ssl = false` in the `[llm]` section for self-signed certificates. |
